premises.text: CPG marketers waste ~50% of huge ad/coupon budgets because they cannot target converters vs already-loyal buyers or reward loyalty properly
premises.evidence_span: they know 50% of that budget is misspent and wasted on the wrong customers

premises.text: Industry still relies on mass printed coupons; Snapdragon aims to reinvent CPG marketing like social/local disruption did for other ads
premises.evidence_span: an industry that still prints millions upon millions of coupons

premises.text: Snapdragon is a product check-in game: scan barcodes, share socially, see friends' opinions at purchase time, and compete on Fanship leaderboards
premises.evidence_span: Snapdragon is a product check-in game with a twist

premises.text: Twist: sarcastic dragon quips and comic-book adventures unlocked by product/check-in combinations hook users
premises.evidence_span: it's the twist that's going to get people hooked

premises.text: Gives CPG marketers targeting tools wrapped in a fun gaming experience
premises.evidence_span: giving consumer product marketers the targeting tools that they need, and wrapping the whole thing in this fun gaming experience

domains.name: product check-in game with comic twist

value.text: Fundamentally reinvent how consumer product companies market to customers via targeted, fun product check-ins
value.evidence_span: fundamentally reinvent how consumer product companies market to their customers

causal_links.evidence_span: This is the opportunity here for disruption
product check-ins that unlock a comic book adventure

notes: Coke/Pepsi coupon examples folded into targeting-waste problem (§4.1.6). Check-in/social/Fanship cascade folded into game product; comic/quips kept as the twist mechanism speaker flags as hook (§4.1.5 split). Marketer targeting benefit folded with product as claimed value path. $2.2T market ownership aspiration not a separate premise (§4.1.4).
